title: First-session starter pack and telemetry runlog
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact working pack for the first 60–90 minutes of a dev's experience when they try Redwood SDK for the first time. Target audience: backend/frontend engineers who want to wire the SDK into a tiny demo or prototype within an hour.

Why this exists (problem):
- Current quickstarts are fragmented across slides, long cookbooks, and example repos.
- New users often stall on API key setup, local env wiring, or not having immediate signal that their requests are succeeding.
- We need a lightweight, observable, repeatable path that shows immediate value and captures telemetry to inform DX improvements.

What this pack contains (high level):
1) 10-minute checklist: account, API key, minimal curl test + expected response snippets.
2) 30-minute guided lab: Node + Python minimal server + single endpoint that calls Redwood for chat or embedding.
3) 30-minute stretch: add a client-side fallback (local stub) and a tiny latency budget dashboard.
4) Telemetry runlog: concrete probes and suggested metrics for the first 1k requests.
5) Failure-mode notes and recovery recipes for common friction.

10-minute checklist (first-run ritual):
- Create free dev account (link in console onboarding banner).
- Create API key scoped to demo-project. Note: encourage ephemeral keys for labs.
- Export env vars: REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ENV=devplayground
- Quick curl smoke test (shell):
  curl -s -X POST 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-mini-1","input":"Hello from the quickstart"}'
  Expected: JSON with top-level 'output' and 'latency_ms' fields. If you get 401 -> key missing; 422 -> malformed body.

30-minute guided lab: minimal server examples
- Goal: Send a single prompt, render response, show latency and request id.
- Node example (express): start server, route POST /ask -> calls Redwood generate API, writes response + X-Request-ID header into UI.
- Python example (Flask/FastAPI): same flow; package examples in /examples/miniserver.
- Emphasize idempotent local-dev runs: use a sandbox model and a cached stub.

Starter snippets to include in quickstart repo: (concise)
- SDK init: 
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
- call: 
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-mini-1', input: 'Summarize this sentence' });
  console.log(res.output, res.latency_ms, res.request_id);
- Advice: add try/catch around client.generate and surface request_id in logs.

Telemetry runlog (what to collect in the first 1k requests):
- Success rate (200s vs 4xx/5xx) per route/sample app.
- P50/P95/P99 latency (generation token time and full roundtrip).
- Cold-start vs warm latency tags (if available from runtime).
- Distribution of model choices (mini vs base vs quantized variant).
- Error taxonomy counts: rate-limited, auth-fail, model-invocation errors, decode-timeouts.
- First-character-of-response length and truncation indicators for early quality signals.

Suggested lightweight telemetry probes (can be implemented from client):
- Emit event: {event: 'request.sent', model, sample_scenario, timestamp} -> on response emit request.finished with request_id, latency_ms, http_status, error_code.
- For front-end demos: track perceived time-to-first-token (TTFT) via streaming handshake.
- For SDK team: surface bundling/pack versions used by first-run cohort.

Landing dashboard (minimal):
- Top row: success rate, 95th latency, avg cost per request (approx), total requests.
- Middle: small time-series of errors with clickable request_id leading to raw logs (console/tracing link).
- Bottom: sample responses with user captions and a small checkbox for quality feedback.

30-minute stretch (resilience + fallback):
- Provide a tiny local stub that returns canned responses (for network-offline demos).
- Show how to configure client to fallback to stub if latency > 1200ms or status >= 500.
- Add a canary toggled via feature-flag env var to simulate degraded prod.

Failure-mode cheat sheet (common causes + quick fixes):
- 401 Authorization: check REDWOOD_API_KEY, verify key hasn't been rotated.
- 429 Rate limit: recommend local throttling or use a smaller model in config.
- 503 Transient capacity: retry with exponential backoff, show circuit-breaker sample.
- Malformed request: use our request validator script (link to tools/validate-request).
- Unhelpful output: include prompt template with examples and recommended guardrails (stop tokens, max_tokens, temperature defaults).

Open questions and unresolved items (notes to self / next steps):
- Should the quickstart create auto-instrumented spans to our tracing backend by default? privacy implications for demo accounts.
- Do we add an opt-in telemetry consent checkbox in the demo flow? (legal wants eyeballs)
- Can we provide a single-file reproducible demo (zero deps) that still demonstrates streaming? Might be tricky.
- Hook into 'first-run' onboarding email flow to ask for feedback after 3 successful requests. Who owns that? Growth?

Testing and gating for merge to main:
- Smoke tests: curl test + node example start + single request pass.
- Integration tests: forked run against sandbox model and assert expected shape of output and headers.
- UX review: short playtest with 3 internal engineers (scripted) to validate friction points.

Launch checklist (pre-merge):
- [ ] Examples repo created and CI enabled.
- [ ] Minimal dashboard prototype ready and linked.
- [ ] Telemetry probes implemented and flagged (opt-in via env).
- [ ] Legal sign-off on demo telemetry contract.
- [ ] Docs: short README + one-pager quickwalk (<= 600 words).

Appendix: quick commands and shortcuts (paste into terminal)
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-xxx
- curl smoke: see above
- start node example: cd examples/miniserver/node && npm ci && npm start
- run python example: cd examples/miniserver/py && pip install -r requirements.txt && uvicorn app:app --reload

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally terse and workshop-friendly. I want the team to try it in a 1-hour internal session and report three friction points.
- Prefer to keep the minimal quickstart as a single-folder artifact that can be copied into hackathon repos.

Hand-off: Riley will pair with Maya for the examples, Devon will own telemetry probe hooks, Priya will coordinate legal/consent language.

History: created as a lightweight response to repeated onboarding feedback threads (slack #devexp, thread: "first-run friction map").

-- end of note --
